summary: Flathead County lookout site with an L-4 cab dated 1930 and listed abandoned and gone; a 1912 phone-line item mentions a lookout man. No source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Cab listed as abandoned and gone per firelookout.com; no source we read describes what remains at the site today

events.note: Lookout man stationed on Moran mountain, with a telephone line to the Moran ranger station (The Columbian, quoted on Forest Lookouts)

evidence.supports: L-4 cab dated 1930; listed as abandoned and gone
site listed under the Flathead National Forest
lookout man stationed on Moran mountain with telephone link to the station
evidence.quote: which gives the lookout man stationed there, telephone communication direct to the station

evidence.supports: telephone connections run from the Moran ranger station
evidence.quote: The forest service has now telephone connections from Moran ranger station to Belton

evidence.supports: second lookout about twenty miles north
evidence.quote: Twenty miles north from there another lookout man is stationed.

evidence.supports: second lookout signals the exact location of a fire to the Moran mountain lookout man
evidence.quote: In case of a fire he signals the exact location of the same to the man on Moran mountain

evidence.supports: page carries a bare Removed label with no date
Montana list marks the site as a ground lookout that is gone

notes_for_editor: Thin: two lookout pages and one list; the 1930 date is firelookout.com's alone and the abandonment year is not given, so no abandoned event is recorded. The 1912 item says 'Moran mountain'; the story hedges that this is the same site, which the Forest Lookouts entry covers. The bare 'Removed' label sits right after the Moran Peak entry on the Forest Lookouts page, with no date or explanation. The Ron Kemnow credit does not appear on the Forest Lookouts page, so it was dropped from the sources. A search snippet mentioned a Moran Patrol Cabin at Coal Ridge (about 8 miles southwest of Polebridge) and a map label giving 7,411 feet for Moran Peak; neither was read or used, and the 7,404 ft figure differs from that map label. No photo found.
